record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: For composite media where microscopic gradients of the local fields can become infinite, how can singularity theory be extended beyond well-developed two-dimensional scalar elliptic cases to three-dimensional problems and elliptic systems, especially the elasticity system, with usable criteria for when singularities occur?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a composite medium occupying a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ consisting of two or more constituent phases separated by interfaces that may have corners, edges, or cusps. Local physical fields (such as the displacement $u$ in linear elasticity, or a scalar potential in a conductivity problem) satisfy an elliptic system inside each phase together with transmission conditions across the interfaces. In the elasticity case, $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^3$ solves
$$\nabla\cdot\big(C(x)\,e(u)\big)=0,\qquad e(u)=\tfrac12(\nabla u+\nabla u^{\mathsf T}),$$
where the elasticity tensor $C(x)$ is piecewise constant, taking distinct values $C^{(i)}$ on each phase. One says that the gradient field exhibits a microscopic singularity at an interface point $x_0$ if $|\nabla u(x)|\to\infty$ as $x\to x_0$.

For the two-dimensional scalar elliptic case (e.g. $\nabla\cdot(\sigma(x)\nabla u)=0$ with piecewise-constant $\sigma$), a rather complete theory exists describing exactly when and with what asymptotic exponents such gradient blow-up occurs at interface corners, depending on the contrast and the geometry.

Problem. Develop an analogous singularity theory for the following two settings, and in each case provide explicit, verifiable criteria (in terms of the geometry of the interface and the contrast in the material coefficients) that determine whether $|\nabla u|$ blows up at a given interface point and, if so, the leading asymptotic behaviour:

(a) scalar elliptic transmission problems $\nabla\cdot(\sigma(x)\nabla u)=0$ posed in three space dimensions, where interfaces may carry edges, conical points, and vertex-edge intersections;

(b) elliptic systems in two and three dimensions, with the linear elasticity system as the principal case, including transmission problems where the elasticity tensor jumps across interfaces having corners, edges, or conical points.

In particular, identify the threshold conditions on the contrast between the $C^{(i)}$ and on the opening angles or solid-angle data of the interface at which singular exponents cross prescribed thresholds (e.g. integrability of $\nabla u$), and give a usable classification of the possible singular behaviours.
artifact.status_search_result: A substantial literature treats stress singularities in three-dimensional elastic composites at corners, edges, wedges, and inclusion tips (asymptotic expansions, eigenvalue problems on solid angles, numerical eigenanalysis, multi-material wedge formulations). However, a complete and unified singularity theory comparable to the 2D scalar case—giving sharp, geometry-and-contrast-based criteria for blow-up and classification of singular exponents for general 3D scalar transmission problems and for elliptic systems including elasticity—does not appear to have been fully established; the problem is partially solved, with many specific cases (planar wedges, axisymmetric corners, particular laminate geometries) understood and active ongoing work in general settings.

status_evidence.title: Singularities near three-dimensional corners in composite laminates
status_evidence.snippet: 3D corner effects in laminates that cannot be captured by 2D analysis; eigenvalue problem for singularity exponents.
status_evidence.claim: 3D composite corner singularities are studied case by case rather than via a complete general theory.

status_evidence.title: On the three-dimensional singular stress field near the corner front of revolution-shaped inclusions
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of 3D singular stress fields near corner fronts of inclusions in elastic composites.
status_evidence.claim: Specific 3D inclusion-corner singularities have been analyzed, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: A Mathematical Analogy and a Unified Asymptotic Formulation for Singular Elastic and Electromagnetic Fields at Multimaterial Wedges
status_evidence.snippet: Unified asymptotic formulation for singular elastic fields at multi-material wedges.
status_evidence.claim: Unified frameworks exist for wedge-type configurations but not for fully general 3D interface geometries.

status_evidence.title: Analytical and Numerical Methods for Analysis of Stress Singularity in 3D Elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms for power-law singular exponents at 3D singular points for isotropic, anisotropic and FGM bodies.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical eigenanalysis is the prevailing approach in 3D, suggesting absence of fully explicit general criteria.
